verdict.rationale: Vercel documents a project configuration file, vercel.json, that sets deployment settings such as regions and per-function overrides. Because the file can live in a Git-connected repo, it is versioned and deployed on every push. Evidence shows only narrow slices of infrastructure defined there, not the whole architecture in one file. Missing for 10: evidence that a single file declares the entire architecture (storage/databases, environments, domains, firewall, marketplace services), documented schema breadth for vercel.json, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a devops-lead, I can define, deploy, and version my entire architecture with a single configuration file

citations.quote: You can override regions for individual functions using the functions property in your project configuration.
Run any code and library on Vercel Functions with an OCI container image built from a Dockerfile or Containerfile at the project root.
Connect GitHub, GitLab, or Bitbucket to deploy on every push, with a preview URL for every branch.
